name: Museum of Modern Belarusian Statehood
funding: A branch of the state National Historical Museum of Belarus, created by the Ministry of Culture and opened in 2012. State bodies lent exhibits to its 4,000-item collection.
watch: Six halls on Belarus since 1990, with the first presidential decrees, gifts to Alexander Lukashenko and models of state buildings, in the Presidential Administration building.

propaganda.summary: The Ministry of Culture opened the museum in 2012 inside the Presidential Administration to present the presidential state since 1994, with Lukashenko's first decrees and gifts to him; he called its opening politically important.

name: AfricaMuseum (Royal Museum for Central Africa)
funding: One of Belgium's ten federal scientific institutes, under the Secretary of State for Federal Science Policy. Two thirds of staff and budget go to research. Bart Ouvry is director general.
watch: The museum had 106,000 visitors in 2024, down from 132,000 in 2023; it occupies the Charles Girault palace inaugurated by King Albert I in 1910.

propaganda.summary: King Leopold II created the museum in 1898 from the 1897 Brussels exposition's colonial section as a propaganda tool for his Congo colonial project; the 1910 building was opened to display the Belgian Congo.

name: Museo de la Revolución Democrática y Cultural
funding: Built by the Fondo Nacional de Inversión Productiva y Social (FPS) for nearly 50 million bolivianos. In 2023 the culture minister said the FPS and Andamarca municipality still administer it.
watch: Opened in 2017 in Evo Morales's birthplace, a village of about 163 people; 17,000 visitors in its first year, and closed since 2020.

propaganda.summary: Evo Morales's government opened the state-built museum in his birthplace in 2017 to show his life, the gifts he received and his achievements. Critics called it a personality cult; it closed after his 2019 fall.

name: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum
funding: Run by Cambodia's Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts, which lists it among its institutions. Foreign adults pay $5 and Cambodians enter free, the museum states.
watch: Former Khmer Rouge prison S-21. Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2025 as part of the Cambodian Memorial Sites.

propaganda.summary: Vietnamese authorities appointed Mai Lam to turn S-21 into a museum in 1979. Rachel Hughes finds the Kampuchean Ministry of Culture, Information and Propaganda oversaw it and used foreign visits to support the regime's legitimacy.

name: Win-Win Memorial
funding: The 12 million dollar memorial was paid mostly by Phnom Penh Municipal Hall, the rest by tycoon Ly Yong Phat, who gave the land. The Defence Ministry solicited public donations.
watch: Inaugurated by Hun Sen on 29 December 2018 in Chroy Changvar; General Nem Sowath's construction committee runs the site and its museum.

propaganda.summary: Hun Sen's government built the memorial, opened 2018, to honour his win-win policy; carvings depict his political triumphs including the 2017 dissolution of the opposition CNRP, and the museum shows his achievements.

name: Great Northern Arts Festival
funding: Canadian Heritage granted CAD 160,000 for 2025 to 2027; the Town of Inuvik gives the venue and over CAD 30,000 in kind. Indigenous bodies, Air North and Northwestel help; Canada Council refused about CAD 90,000 in 2026.
watch: Imperial Oil and ConocoPhillips stopped funding it in 2015 when they shelved Arctic exploration, and programming was cut.
records_note: Names its sponsors and what each gives, without amounts.

name: Pitquhirnikkut Ilihautiniq / Kitikmeot Heritage Society (May Hakongak Cultural Centre)
funding: Canadian Heritage granted CAD 162,608 for 2025 to 2027. CanNor gave CAD 766,018 toward the CAD 1.7M Kuugalak workspace, planned with Nunavut Tunngavik, Nunavut, federal and Indigenous Clean Energy money.
watch: Runs the May Hakongak cultural centre and library; the Kuugalak workspace adds room for Inuinnaqtun language courses.
records_note: Federal grants are listed in Canada's open grants register.

name: Chairman Mao Memorial Hall
funding: Established on 8 October 1976 by joint decision of the CCP Central Committee, the NPC Standing Committee, the State Council and the Central Military Commission. Entry is free.
watch: Opened 9 September 1977 in Tiananmen Square; 240 million visitors, among them over 190 heads of state. Memorial rooms for Mao and five other leaders.

propaganda.summary: The Party and state built the hall in 1976 to 1977 to display Mao's embalmed body; the Party designates it a national patriotic education demonstration base.

name: Hong Kong Museum of the War of Resistance and Coastal Defence
funding: Owned and run by the Hong Kong Government's Leisure and Cultural Services Department. Admission to its thematic exhibitions is free.
watch: In the 1887 British Lei Yue Mun Fort; opened in 2000 as the Museum of Coastal Defence and renamed on 3 September 2024.

propaganda.summary: The 2023 Policy Address ordered the Museum of Coastal Defence converted to strengthen national pride and patriotism; the government renamed it on 3 September 2024 as a patriotic education base.

name: Liu Manor Museum (Rent Collection Courtyard)
funding: Run under county-level administration since 1984. Provincial permission was needed for exhibit changes in 1988 (Ho and Li, Modern China, 2016).
watch: The 114 clay figures were made in 1965 by Sichuan Fine Arts Institute artists. Tens of millions visited in the Mao era.

propaganda.summary: Opened in 1959 as an exhibit of the landlord's crimes. Ho and Li report officials fabricated evidence such as a water dungeon, and denounced class enemies faced show trials there in the Cultural Revolution.
